pr_title: Improve rotation in the 3D transform gizmo
pr_body:
The current implementation for rotation transforms has some issues when the rotation axis gets close to being orthogonal with the camera's forward direction.  I changed the way rotation angles are computed and added some special cases for orthogonal rotation axes.

Before:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4402304/150139704-d2008b27-2fcd-4ad8-9f43-fba955151194.mp4




After:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4402304/150139714-86e5923b-1b40-4017-9f05-329f91403a38.mp4


Changes include:
* Get rid of deadzones. Fixes #56582.
* Make it easier to select rotation handles at very oblique angles.
* Handle rotation for axes that are perpendicular to the camera.

Note: This PR will probably create conflicts with #56543. I would merge the other one first, and I can handle the rebase on top of it.

issue_context.title: Rotate tool has deadzone on X axis
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.dev.custom_build.2c7fcdd7f

### System information

Linux 5.15.10-arch1-1

### Issue description

When using the rotate tool and moving the mouse to rotate around the X axis, there is a deadzone where the transform doesn't change and mouse movements don't seem to be registered.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2496231/148322454-e8aa5115-bec2-42f3-ac09-b625a172ed18.mp4


### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a MeshInstance
2. Activate the rotate tool
3. Grab the X (red) handle
4. Move the mouse in a circle around the object in the 3D view

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments:
Gizmo was recently updated, and I thought that might have caused the regression, but this problem seems to be unrelated as it occurs whether it is merged or not.

My feeling is that it seems like the dead zone is caused by distance. In other words, if the rotation axis is close enough to the object, it will rotate correctly. My guess is that something invisible like the YZ plane (afaik, the hit decision was procedurally calculated in EditorPlugin), is causing the dead zone.
@akien-mga It's not regression, there is same issue in 3.x.

review_comments:
This struct seems to be used only once, why does it have different init in the header and in the class constructor?

All this could be set to the right values in the header directly I think.
Historic reasons, I guess. I did think about cleaning this up, but I thought it can wait after alpha2, just in case.
